challenges.name: visibility-timeout-quiz
challenges.title: Why did the grading job run twice?
challenges.description: Two pieces of evidence from the grading queue: the worker logs of the duplicated submission, and a heartbeat added to a worker that grades in its own process.

questions.question:
Queue attribute: VisibilityTimeout = 60 (seconds). Worker logs:

12:00:00.012 grader-1 received sub_4471 receiveCount=1
12:01:00.031 grader-2 received sub_4471 receiveCount=2
12:01:10.144 grader-1 graded sub_4471 in 70.1 s -> result r_9001
12:01:10.162 grader-1 DeleteMessage sub_4471 (receipt from 12:00:00) -> 200
12:02:10.377 grader-2 graded sub_4471 in 70.3 s -> result r_9002
12:02:10.391 grader-2 DeleteMessage sub_4471 (receipt from 12:01:00) -> 200

The graders do not call ChangeMessageVisibility.

Statement: "The delivery to grader-2 at 12:01:00 is the queue working as configured: grader-1 had neither deleted the message nor extended its visibility within 60 seconds of receiving it."
questions.explanation: True. Receiving a message hides it for the visibility timeout; it is not handed over for good. Grader-1 received it at 12:00:00 and its delete only came at 12:01:10, after the 60-second lease had ended, and it never extended the lease. At 12:01:00 the message was visible again, so the next receive delivered it with a receive count of 2 and a new receipt handle. The queue cannot tell a slow worker from a dead one. The fix is on the configuration and worker side: a timeout above the measured p99 of the jobs, a heartbeat that extends the lease while the work is alive, and an idempotent result write. The misconception is that a redelivery is a queue bug; it is the mechanism that recovers jobs from crashed workers.

False. setInterval callbacks run on the event loop, and runTestsSync keeps the event loop busy for the whole 70 seconds, so the timer cannot fire until the tests are done: the missing "heartbeat" lines prove it. The lease is never extended, ends at 60 seconds, and a second worker can receive the message, exactly as before. BullMQ's automatic lock renewal fails the same way, which shows up as stalled jobs. CPU-bound work has to run outside the event loop (a worker thread, a child process, a sandboxed processor or a separate service) for a heartbeat to work. The misconception is that scheduling a timer guarantees it runs on time; in Node.js it runs only when the event loop is free.

challenges.name: visibility-timeout-queue
challenges.title: Build the lease: receive, ack, extend and redeliver
challenges.description: CodeDev's grading queue ran a 70-second job twice because its visibility timeout is 60 seconds, and an old delivery's ack could act on a message that a newer delivery was grading. Implement the queue side, class VisibilityQueue(visibilityTimeoutMs), on a fake clock (every method gets `now` in milliseconds). send(id, body, now): the message is visible from now; ids are unique. receive(now): among messages visible at or before now, take the one that became visible earliest (ties: sent first), add 1 to its receive count, issue the receipt handle "<id>#<receiveCount>", hide it until now + visibilityTimeoutMs and return { messageId, body, receiptHandle, receiveCount }; return null when none is visible. ack(receiptHandle, now): delete the message and return true only if the handle is current, meaning it is the latest handle issued for a message that still exists (it stays valid after the timeout passed, until the message is received again); otherwise return false and change nothing. extendVisibility(receiptHandle, timeoutMs, now): only for a current handle whose message is still hidden (now < the time it becomes visible), hide it until now + timeoutMs and return true; timeoutMs 0 makes it visible at once. Return false and change nothing if the handle is not current, the message is visible again, or timeoutMs is not a whole number from 0 to 43200000. The runner simulates workers that poll, work for each message's workMs, send heartbeats, crash, and make extra client calls. Input: { visibilityTimeoutMs, untilMs, messages: [{ id, at, workMs }], workers: [{ name, pollMs, heartbeatMs?, extendMs? }], crashes?: [{ message, delivery, afterMs }], calls?: [{ at, ack? | extend?, timeoutMs? }] }. Output: { deliveries (receives per message), rejectedAcks, remaining (not deleted), log }.
hints: For each stored message, what must the queue remember so that it can answer two questions at any time: is it visible at `now`, and which receipt handle is allowed to act on it?

Look at what receive changes (receive count, current handle, the time the message becomes visible), and make ack and extendVisibility start with the same check: find the message from the handle and compare the handle with the latest one issued. extendVisibility has two more conditions: the message is still hidden, and timeoutMs is valid.

A worked trace with a 30,000 ms timeout: send m at 0. receive(0) gives m#1, hidden until 30,000. extendVisibility("m#1", 30000, 20000) is true: hidden until 50,000. receive(49999) is null; receive(50000) gives m#2. Now ack("m#1", 51000) is false, extendVisibility("m#1", 1000, 51000) is false, and ack("m#2", 90000) is true even though m#2's lease ended at 80,000, because nobody received m again.
